title: Intestinal stem cells count self-renewal divisions to switch multipotency.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: paper_context.py: no PMCID, not open access in Europe PMC, no supplement, no text-mined accessions. NCBI elink from PMID 42527588 returns only related-PubMed links (no GEO, SRA or BioProject). Zenodo search on the title returned 0 records; GEO keyword search returned 0. Nature article page redirects to a login (paywalled), so the data availability statement could not be read. One web search found no preprint or deposited dataset.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the study design comes from the abstract: Drosophila ISC (intestinal stem cell) lineage tracing showing eight EC-producing divisions between EMC (enteroendocrine mother cell) divisions, and histone-mark (H3K4me3, H3K36me3, H3K27me3) imaging across divisions. No sample sizes or file formats were visible.

a1_downloadable.note: No deposited dataset found: no GEO/SRA/BioProject link from PubMed, nothing on Zenodo, paper paywalled with no Europe PMC full text or supplement. Any source data sits behind the Nature paywall and is unverified.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The measurements are per-clone division counts and histone-mark intensities from microscopy; any prediction label (e.g. division number or fate at next division) would have to be built from images or lineage scoring. Judged from the abstract only.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs would be confocal images or hand-scored lineage tracks, none of which were found deposited.

a5_enough_rows.note: Row count unknown. Lineage-tracing studies of this kind typically yield tens to hundreds of clones, likely below the 400-row classification bar, but this was not verified.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Not checkable; any source-data spreadsheets would be small.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No files to compare against the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels would be direct experimental observations (lineage counts, immunostaining), not model output; not verified in files.

backbone.name: none applicable (fly lineage imaging; no sequence or single-cell matrix found)

honest_claim_h3: No ML claim is possible: no accessible measurement table was found, and the paper's findings are a mechanistic lineage-tracing result, not a dataset.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use histone-mark levels measured in fly gut stem cells to predict how many divisions remain before the next switch in daughter cell type.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-stem-cell measurements of active and repressive histone marks plus division history from lineage tracing; number of examples unknown because no data were found.
plain_idea.predict: The division count since the last enteroendocrine-producing division (or whether the next division switches fate), scored by the authors from lineage tracing in the microscope.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would test whether chromatin state alone reads out the division counter; but with the hard-coded count of eight, a simple threshold rule likely suffices, so ML adds little.

ml_idea: Considered: predict division-count position or upcoming fate switch from per-cell histone-mark intensities. Not viable: no deposited data, likely small n, and the relationship is a near-deterministic threshold that a single-feature rule captures.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; no data files located.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Find a deposited dataset (GEO/Zenodo/BioImage Archive) for PMID 42527588; none found via NCBI elink or Zenodo, which kills it.

verdict_reason: Fails A1: paywalled Drosophila lineage-tracing paper with no deposited data found (no NCBI repository links, nothing on Zenodo, no open full text). Any label would have to be built from microscopy, and n is likely small.
